target_customer: Car owners (including parents of teen drivers) who want to monitor a car remotely
problem: Owners cannot see where their car is or how it is driven when they are away; Drive Pulse sold an always-on OBD-II device with cellular data and an iPhone app.
business_model: Hardware sale (about 69.99 dollars) plus monthly subscription (about 6.99 dollars) per a 2013 era article
product_category: Connected car OBD-II telematics device and app

founders.name: Giancarlo Daniele
founders.background_notes: YC page labels him YC W13 founder while the company page lists batch Winter 2014; a search result calls him a Stanford graduate in his early 20s, not verified from an opened source.

competitors.name: Automatic
competitors.what: Bluetooth OBD-II adapter plus iPhone app logging trips, MPG and driving behavior
competitors.traction_then: Still in beta in August 2013, priced at about 70 dollars

technical_complexity.rationale: Required custom OBD-II hardware with cellular connectivity and an iPhone app; the listing said it needed adequate T-Mobile coverage.

defensibility.rationale: OBD-II dongles with apps were already shipping from Automatic and others and no data or network moat is described.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rivals kept shipping; Automatic raised later rounds and was bought by Sirius XM in 2017 per Dealroom. No source describes what happened to Drive Pulse.

market_need_then: Connected car adapters were a visible category in 2013 and 2014, with rival coverage and later funding of Zubie and Automatic, but no sources show demand for Drive Pulse itself.

branding.domain_note: Used drivepulseapp.com, a suffixed domain; it later became an unrelated electrical referral site.

brand_strength.rationale: Search results show many unrelated products named DrivePulse, Driver Pulse and Drive Motors, and no press on the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Drive Pulse was a one founder YC Winter 2014 hardware and app company with a cellular OBD-II device. No funding, traction, shutdown date or cause was found beyond the YC Inactive status, and its website now hosts an unrelated business, so the cause of failure is not public.
notes: Outcome, funding and funding cross-check searches returned no article about Drive Pulse itself; Crunchbase, CB Insights and VCBacked pages appeared with no figures. CB Insights puts it in Northampton, England with 2013 founding and VCBacked says Stanford; these conflict and are unverified. Pricing and founder details came from search summaries of third party pages (theinternetpatrol.com). drivepulseapp.com now shows an Escondido electrical referral site, unrelated. No dated competitor beyond Automatic was found; Zubie and Dash dates were not verified.
